# Counts

Every oracle fixture, input fixtures included, built counted (`adamic build --count`, runtime/count.h) and run once. Counts are deterministic, so a
change to how Adamic counts references shows here as a change of numbers, in review. Allocations and frees are heap values (strings,
objects, arrays, maps, cells, closures); retains and releases are calls to adamic_retain and adamic_release; peak is the most heap
values live at once; in regions is the values let go of with their region (runtime/region.c) rather than freed one at a time, so a
finished program's allocations are its frees and its values in regions. A fixture that panics is counted where it stopped; an input
fixture runs as TestInputAgreesWithNode runs it, a directory of its own to write in included, and must finish. Every run has an
8 MiB stack (ulimit -s 8192), so a fixture's counts never depend on the stack of whoever runs it. This is the baseline borrow
inference and reuse in place are measured against (docs/memory.md).

Not counted, though the oracle runs it as it runs every fixture: internal/oracle/testdata/stack_overflow.a, which recurses until
the stack runs out, so its allocations measure how deep it got, and every change to a frame's size moves them; and
internal/oracle/testdata/moves/accepted/objects.a, whose counted build alone is over a unit's 60 s (the moves tests hold it
to Node and the leak check).

The tree build measures each row once for what it runs (its emitted C, how an input fixture runs and the files it reads, the
runtime's sources, the counted build's flags and the clang that builds it), into a product keyed by exactly that
(TestProduct_CountMeasurements), and every run holds every row to its measurement; a fixed tenth (countsSampleSeed) is measured
again in the run itself. So a change that moves what rows run but not their counts changes no line here.

Generated by TestCountsAreRecorded; after a change that moves them, run
`go test ./internal/oracle -run TestCountsAreRecorded -args -update-counts` and commit the diff.

| Fixture | Allocations | Frees | Retains | Releases | Peak live | In regions |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|

## Predicate direction counts

Each overload witness is loaded from a temporary .ts copy: checked admission is
explicit, while its stored .a source remains a Node witness. True directions are
checked once; false directions are checked where the checker excludes part of the
incoming type. Assertions have an asserts direction. Unobservable directions are
reported separately and are not body proofs. These are compiler proof counts,
independent of the runtime allocation counts above.

| Fixture | Call sites | Proven | Checked | Unobservable |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|

## Files and updates

Runtime records live in `runtime/<repository-relative-fixture-path>.counts`; predicate
records live in `predicates/<repository-relative-fixture-path>.counts`. Each file contains
one complete row and one LF newline. The source extension is retained to distinguish
`.a` and `.ts` fixtures. Paths and decimal counts contain no host, timestamp, line-ending
or toolchain-dependent serialization. The house measurement compiler is clang 20.1.8.

Input fixtures and explicit frontend adapters use the same runtime mirror, keyed by
their existing source path. The planted runtime row is
`runtime/dedication/dedication.a.counts`. The former predicate table is split too, one
file per predicate fixture under `predicates/`; it has no shared changing index.

Run `go test ./internal/oracle -run TestCountsAreRecorded -count=1 -args -update-counts`
after count changes and commit only the moved records. A selective shard update keeps
unmeasured records. Remove a record when removing its counted fixture: the census
rejects missing and orphan records. Refused, NotYet, and the documented uncounted
fixtures remain outside the runtime count registry, as before this migration.

Committed records are independent expected values. Tests compare actual measurements
with them; ordinary runs never rewrite them. The determinism shards regenerate current
measurement products into a temporary directory with the same writer used by
`-update-counts`, then compare bytes with the committed files. Predicate regeneration
does the same from the compiler's independent proof counts.
